result.title: AdaC-GRPO: Towards Mastering Long-Horizon Visual Sudoku Puzzles via Adaptive Curriculum Learning
result.summary: While reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR) enhances reasoning in large language models, its efficacy in long-horizon multimodal tasks remains underexplored. Visual Sudoku puzzles pose a representative challenge, requiring multi-step deductive reasoning over both local constraints and global dependency chains. To this end, we introduce FG-Sudoku, a fine-grained benchmark categorized by grid size and required deductive steps. Evaluations reveal that frontier MLLMs fail on complex long-range dependencies (e.g., 9*9 puzzles). During post-training, this near-zero success rate causes severe reward sparsity, halting standard RLVR. We propose Adaptive Curriculum Group Relative Policy Optimization (AdaC-GRPO) to overcome this. Unlike rigid or prior-based schedules, AdaC-GRPO dynamically constructs training batches by tracking the model's "Zone of Proximal Development" via online rollout accuracy. Experiments demonstrate that AdaC-GRPO enables Qwen2.5-VL-7B to approach the performance of Gemini-2.5-Flash while bridging 62.2% of the overall accuracy gap to Gemini-2.5-Pro, with its generalizability further validated across InternVL-3.5 and Qwen3-VL.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建按网格规模与推理步数分级的视觉数独基准 FG-Sudoku，指出前沿 MLLM 在长程依赖上近乎零成功率导致奖励稀疏，并提出 AdaC-GRPO，依据在线 rollout 准确率跟踪「最近发展区」动态构造训练批次。
AI.relevance_reason: 面向 VLM 长程多步视觉推理的训练与评测，其奖励稀疏诊断与按能力动态调度难度的思路，可供核查 LVR 中轨迹训练、监督信号与长度泛化问题；但未涉及内部 latent 状态的生成与使用。
